summary.short: Amends Law 5651: defines social network providers, sets fines, and requires providers with over one million daily Turkish users to appoint a local representative, report, respond to requests within 48 hours and host Turkish users' data locally, with escalating sanctions. Social network provisions apply from 1 October 2020.
summary.long: Law No. 7253 amends Law No. 5651 on internet publications. It defines 'social network provider' (Art. 1), allows fines to be notified to providers abroad (Art. 2), and raises one fine from 100,000 to 1,000,000 Turkish lira (Art. 3). It extends the content-removal and access-blocking provisions (Arts. 4-5). The new Additional Article 4 covers social network providers with more than one million daily accesses from Turkey, domestic or foreign: they must appoint and notify a representative in Turkey, answer user applications on content within 48 hours, submit statistical reports every six months and take measures to store Turkish users' data in Turkey. Non-compliance leads to escalating administrative fines (10 and then 30 million lira), a ban on new advertising by Turkish taxpayers, and bandwidth reduction of up to 90% ordered by a criminal judgeship of peace. Providers that fail to remove content within 24 hours of notice of a court decision are liable for damages. The definition and Additional Article 4 apply from 1 October 2020; other provisions from publication.

notes: Amending act: Art. 3, 4 and 5 amend Law 5651 by replacing wording, and Art. 2 adds a paragraph; the text restates no full articles.
